text:
Marathon's stock bounced back 4.6% today after plunging nearly 17% over the past two weeks, driven partly by stabilization in oil markets and a modest recovery in refinery operations. The company had cratered in early November following its earnings report on November 3rd, but today's gain reflects a temporary rebound as US crude held above $99 per barrel and refineries maintained high utilization at 94.5%—conditions that support refiner margins and profitability.

The sharp decline earlier this week appears tied to the earnings miss or disappointing guidance from the November 3rd report, which overshadowed any benefit from stable refining conditions. With geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Iran negotiations stalled, per today's news) potentially supporting oil prices longer-term, the stock's recovery today suggests some investors see the sell-off as overdone, though the stock remains well below its level from a week ago.
